Support Triage for Messages That Mention Self-Harm

Last reviewed February 2026 by Support Operations and Trust & Safety

Scope: This internal guide helps Meridian support agents route tickets that mention self-harm or immediate personal safety concerns. It is not a substitute for crisis care, mental-health support, emergency services, or legal advice.

Messages that mention self-harm require careful handling, fast escalation, and clear boundaries. Agents should avoid improvised advice, avoid minimizing the message, and follow the escalation steps below exactly as written.

When to use this guide

  • Use it when a user message directly mentions self-harm, suicide, or immediate personal danger.
  • Use it only for support triage and escalation.
  • If local emergency risk appears immediate, follow the emergency escalation path before any product troubleshooting.

Required response steps

  1. Acknowledge the message in calm, non-judgmental language.
  2. Escalate immediately to the duty lead and Trust & Safety queue.
  3. Use the approved crisis-response template rather than free-form advice.
  4. Pause normal product troubleshooting until the safety escalation is complete.

Documentation and limits

Keep notes factual and brief. Do not speculate about the person’s mental state. Record what was said, what escalation path was used, and which approved template was sent. If regional emergency guidance is unclear, escalate to the incident lead rather than guessing.
